_comment: ScrollKiller guilt pack. Bundled in assets/ today; the shape is deliberately the one a
server would return so a future /guilt_pack fetch can hot-swap it with no app update.
See docs/DECISIONS.md D9 and D33.
Contract the loader enforces (GuiltPackParser):
schema_version  int  — loader REJECTS anything it doesn't know and keeps the pack it
already has. Bump only for a breaking shape change.
revision        int  — monotonic content version. A remote pack must have a HIGHER
revision than the installed one to replace it (stale-write guard).
lines[].id      str  — STABLE and unique. It is the rotation's no-repeat key, so
reusing an id for different text makes a line look 'already seen'.
lines[].weight  int  — relative pick odds within the eligible pool. >=1. A line at
weight 4 is twice as likely as one at weight 2.
lines[].category str — must be one of the four below; a line with an unknown category
is DROPPED, not fatal, so a newer server pack degrades gracefully
on an older client.
surfaces        map  — which categories each render surface may draw from. This is the
tone policy, and living in the pack means it is remotely tunable
too. Unknown surface keys are ignored; a known surface missing
here falls back to all categories.
Categories:
roast          — playful mockery. The default voice.
existential    — the heavier time-is-finite register. Used sparingly.
reverse_psych  — gives permission to continue, so continuing feels like a choice.
pride          — encouragement for stopping. D9: mixing these in is what keeps the app
from being a shame machine people uninstall. Never remove the category.

lines.text: Your thumb has done more cardio than you have today.
Congratulations — employee of the month, at a company that doesn't pay you.
You've seen this exact video before. It wasn't good then either.
That was a lot of other people's lives. How's yours going?
Your attention span called. It left a voicemail.
Somewhere a book you bought is gathering dust and opinions.
You're not picking these videos. They're picking you.
This is the part where a well-adjusted person stands up.
Still here. Bold strategy.
You opened this app to check one thing. Remember what it was?
That's time you don't get back. Not one second of it.
You'll remember none of this tomorrow. That's the design.
Nothing you just watched will exist in your life next week.
The feed is infinite. You are not.
You came for a minute. The minute is long gone.
Every scroll is a small trade: your life for their ad revenue.
One day you'll want this hour back. Today is that day.
The scroll never ends. Only you can end it.
Nobody reaches the bottom. That's the whole trick.
Go on. One more. See if it fixes anything.
Keep going — the good one is definitely coming up next.
Don't stop now. You're so close to feeling nothing at all.
By all means, continue. The algorithm has notes.
Sure, carry on. It's not like you had plans.
One more won't hurt. That's what the last forty said.
Stay. The exit is boring anyway.
Nobody's stopping you. That's sort of the problem.
You noticed. That's the hard part — the rest is easy.
Closing this is a win. Small, but it counts.
You've stopped before. You can stop now.
Putting it down is a skill. You're practising it right now.
Tomorrow-you is quietly rooting for this decision.
You're not weak for scrolling. You're strong for stopping.
This is the moment you get to choose. Choose well.
Every time you close it, it gets a little easier.
